SA20 passion for cricket

By: Floris Kotze | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Imagine a cricket tournament that’s not just about the game. It’s a show. A celebration. A way to show off South Africa’s talent and spirit.

Unique Selling Point:
This is SA20—our country’s top T20 cricket league. But it’s more than big hits and fireworks. It’s about people and their stories.
One of these fans is now famous, Devino Jacobs, we follow his journey to Paarl grounds to watch Paarl Royals play Durban's Super Giants!

We’ll speak to Graeme Smith, the tournament director. He’s the man behind it all. He tells us first hand how he ended up here, director of the tournament.
He’ll share how SA20 started and why it’s about more than just cricket—it’s about uniting South Africans and creating opportunities.
We weave stories of players in and out of the main story.
Then there’s Codi Yusuf. His cricket career almost ended before it even started. But SA20 gave him a second chance. Now, he’s back, showing that it’s never too late to turn your life around.
And Nqaba Peter—he went from practicing at Border to bowling for the Proteas. His story proves that talent can be found anywhere, even in the most unexpected places.
We’ll go behind the scenes to see the sacrifices, the hard work, and the dreams that keep these players going. It’s not just about the players. It’s about the umpires, the fans, and everyone who makes SA20 special.
We’ll attend a few games and capture our passion for cricket and have some voxies of fans.
Bring in the catches and what fans can win - R1million!
This league isn’t just cricket. And it’s proof that anyone can rise if given the opportunity. That’s what SA20 is all about.
We end the show with our Superfan, Devino - going out of frame happy!

Opening Sequence (1:30)


Visuals: High-energy montage of big hits, run-outs, flashing lights, cheering crowds, and fireworks.
Voice-Over: Something like: “It’s loud, it’s thrilling, it’s cricket like you’ve never seen it before! This is SA20, South Africa’s premier T20 cricket tournament.”
Include snippets of commentators’ calls, crowd reactions, and dynamic music.
Interview Clip (Graeme Smith): A quick soundbite: “SA20 is not just a tournament—it’s a celebration of cricket and talent.”




What is SA20? (2:00)
Visuals: Behind-the-scenes shots of the SA20 organisation—team buses, training sessions, ticket sales, and crowds arriving.
Voice-Over: Something like this: “The SA20 is South Africa’s T20 cricket league, featuring six teams, top players, and a vision to bring cricket to the forefront of our nation’s sporting culture.”
Interview (Graeme Smith): Discuss the tournament’s origins, growth, and its impact on South African cricket.


Deeper Human Stories (6:00) (I would like to see these players with family and friends, if possible)
Voiceover to say something like this: "Although these players are heroes to many, they share a humble beginning—growing up in homes just like ours. The difference? They possess a God-given talent: cricket."
Ottneil Baartman (2:00)
Visuals: Ottneil practicing, interacting with family, and childhood visuals from Oudtshoorn.
Interview (Ottneil & Family)
Says something like “Growing up in Oudtshoorn taught me resilience. Cricket was my escape.”
Voice-Over: Something like this: “From playing street cricket in Oudtshoorn to competing in a World Cup final, Ottneil Baartman’s story is one of resilience and opportunity.”
Highlight Dale Steyn’s mentorship and how it transformed his career.

Codi Yusuf (2:00)
Visuals: Codi training with Paarl Royals, interacting with his wife, and childhood visuals in Florida, Johannesburg.
Interview (Codi & Wife): “SA20 gave me a second chance—not just in cricket but in life.”
Voice-Over: Something like this: “Codi Yusuf’s cricket journey almost ended before it truly began. But SA20 opened the door to a new chapter, both on and off the field.”






A link to the following
Nqaba Peter (2:00)
Nqaba training, footage from his Proteas game, and shots of him bowling the final over in SA20.
Interview (Nqaba): “From Border nets to the Proteas—it’s been a dream I never dared to dream.”
Voice-Over: Something like: “From bowling at the Proteas in practice to becoming one himself, Nqaba Peter’s story is proof that talent can be discovered in the most unexpected places.”






Behind the Scenes: Umpires & Teams (1:30)
Visuals: Umpires preparing, practicing decision-making under pressure, and interacting with players.
Voice-Over: Something like: “They’re the unsung heroes of the game. The umpires, who carry the weight of every decision on their shoulders.”
Interview (Umpire): “The pressure is immense. One wrong call can change everything.”


Closing & Impact (1:00)
Visuals: Crowd celebrations, players hugging, and trophies being lifted.
Voice-Over: “The SA20 is more than cricket—it’s hope, opportunity, and a celebration of South Africa’s talent.”
Interview Clips: Players reflecting on what SA20 means to them.


End Sequence (0:30)
Visuals: Highlights of players, fans, and the tournament atmosphere.
Voice-Over: “This is SA20—where dreams are made, and cricket comes alive....”

6660 SA20 Script

Paarl Opening Shots
Devino VO:
I am excited.
We don't often get a final home game in Paarl.

VO:
My name is Devino Jacobs. I live in Paarl. I am a huge Paarl Royals fan. I can't walk around with no paint. People know me as the paint guy!
I am very nervous because it is our final home game. We are going to give 110 percent tonight even if I have to lose my voice tonight because that how purple and pink my heart is!”

Quick montage of shots:
“We are set for match number 23, Power Royals vs the Durban’s….”

Link:
Devino is definitely someone special, but he's just one of thousands of fans around the country that have come to support their team at the SA20. And that's what this tournament's about. It's about supporting your team, watching exciting cricket, but most of all, it's about the vibe!

Shots
“That's a very good shot. Catch, one-handed catch. Oh, have we got something? I think we have got something.”

VO1:
SA20 has made headlines, big hits, passionate fans and an atmosphere buzzing with energy.
So we headed to Paarl in the Western Cape to see for ourselves.

Link:
When you're this close to the action, it makes you think that you can actually play a team. But my skills stopped at Baker's Cricket.

Graeme Smith
We've been very clear about our ambitions from the start. We've been open. We've been public about wanting to be the biggest league outside of India. With the growth of Franchise Cricket, we really wanted to be the number one player in the Southern Hemisphere.




VO2
SA20 is a professional league with 6 privately owned franchises. Franchise cricket is growing globally with the likes of SA20 and the Indian premier league - the IPL. Unlike traditional domestic cricket, it’s a business—teams sign top local and international players, attract big sponsors, and pack stadiums with fans.

SA20 features six teams battling it out in 34 matches over 5 weeks, all fighting for a spot in the playoffs and, ultimately, the grand final. And the stakes? A massive R70 million in prize money.

At the helm of it all is former Proteas captain Graeme Smith. Now in its third season, HIS team has been working relentlessly to take SA20 to new heights.

Graeme Smith
I remember that first World Cup in 07 in South Africa and then IPL kicked off in 08 and I was a part of both and I couldn't believe how suddenly this format just really captured the imagination.
For cricket to grow into the future, we needed to start introducing new audiences. So outside putting on the best cricketers in the world and the field, we really did try and change things up and create an in-stadium through the TV experience that people thought was fun, new, fresh and would attract anyone really.
There's a product in your own country that people are talking about at a global level.

Upsound
Got him straight through, Maphaka has struck...

Nikhil Uttamchandani
What has been developed here is more than just a cricket tournament. The product has now evolved into people. I mean, for us to be in Paarl on a Monday and to be a sell-out crowd, I think that speaks volumes about what the league has done. It's the league of people, I think.

VO3:
Nikhil Uttamchandani is one of the commentators.

Nikhil uttamchandani
I often when I'm off commentary tend to just go into the crowd and just stand there, sometimes sit, talk to people, talk to the locals, learn some Afrikaans.
It's great man. Yeah, I really enjoy it.

VO4:
But it's not all fun and games. The SA20 also has a serious side. Players aim to impress with hopes of being selected for the IPL, which is often career changing.



Upsound
Oh, there's a shout first up.

VO5:
And making sure the game stays fair, the umpires, often unnoticed, but essential.

Govan
How does umpiring this kind of tournament differ from normal umpiring?

Tom Mokorosi
Yeah, so we've got DRS, which is a big change from our domestic cricket, where players can review umpires' decisions. If you make a mistake, it is corrected.
The right decision is made and the game moves on.
Govan:
But it's also nice and dramatic.
Tom:
The heart rate flies through the roof as soon as they review it. And that first replay comes on. Your onscreen signal now.

Upsound
What a good start for the Durbans, super giants. They picked up Joe Root.

Tom Mokorosi
We don't often umpire for packed stadiums. And it definitely is something we want more of, not less of. And the nervousness is good, nervous energy.

Graeme Smith
One area is our domestic cricket and international cricket. The gap was widening. I think one thing that the SA20 has done is it's closed that gap. You've created almost an international league in South Africa now where our players, both those experienced and young, are being exposed to a platform that hopefully will make them even better cricketers. The other thing is, last year we had the most players picked up at the IPL. And that platform that our players are getting now outside those that played for South Africa, there's a lot that never would have been seen. And now they're being seen and they're getting opportunities globally as well.

VO6:
One of these young players is Paarl Royals bowler Codi Yusuf.

Cody Yousuf
I don't think you can come into any of the games and say this team will win or that team will win. All around this, there's very good players in each of the teams.
Govan
Has the SA20 changed your life at all?

Cody Yousuf
Definitely. It's obviously given me the exposure financially as well. Obviously there's a lot of money that they pumped into this comp and I managed to do things that I couldn't do before I came into this comp. So it definitely changed my life.

VO7:
Nqaba Peter is back for HIS second season with the Paarl Royals.

Nqaba Peter
I never knew at this age I could be such a role model, not just for people younger than me, but also for guys who are even older than me.
All the guys come and tell me, listen man, we watch you every time we play, we're rooting for you, we really look up to you. People have kids who want our kids to be like you one day.
Govan
It's because you represent them. It's very important for black cricket players to get representation time.
Nqaba Peter
I do think there are black players who are talented and skilled enough to be in the SA20.

Graeme Smith
We've worked with Cricket South Africa on the structure.
The amount of money that they're spending on grassroots programs annually, we're supporting them on schools. I think there's definitely been improvements. We are a global league that splits players up. So there's four international players per every team as well, which takes up an immense amount of playing places as well.

It's good to see young black African talent coming through like Maphaka and making that this stage. Every game now we're starting to see really big contributions and hopefully our franchises will recognize that and go from strength to strength.

Link
The IPL showed us how popular T20 cricket can be, but the SA20 is showing that South Africans can do it too.
We certainly have the fans and the vibe!

Upsound:
That's clubbed. That's a very good shot. Catch, one handed catch. Oh, have we got something? I think we have got something.

Link:
So one handed catch while I'm here. That's incredible.



VO8:
Another fan-favorite addition is the one-handed catch competition, with a huge cash prize up for grabs.

The rules are simple—catch the ball with one hand, and you’re in the running. At the end of the tournament, all the successful catchers share the R2 million prize!

Upsound
Oh, he's on his knee and he's clubbed that one and he's hit it for six. What a shot.
Govan
Three to win from two.

VO9:
The win alone was enough to send Devino home smiling, but his night was about to get even more special.

Not only did he meet his hero, Proteas stalwart David Miller—he even got a team shirt.

But knowing Davino, he’ll never wear it…


END

Promo1
VO: Big names, big hits, and six teams fighting to win it all.
Graeme Smith
Platform for them globally is huge because now the whole world's watching this. Instead of 15 players touring for their country, there's now 70 that are getting the opportunity for people around the world to see.
VO: We attended a few games to find out what makes SA20 so popular.

Promo 2
VO: Ever wondered what it takes to run a cricket league? SA20 isn't just about the players. We go behind the scenes to find out what makes this tournament so popular.
Nqaba
I think SA20 has definitely done a lot for young players. This is the second biggest league in the world.

Promos 3
VO: There is a superfan behind every super over! (Alt Take)
Graeme Smith
There's a level of loyalty of the fans to their teams. It's not just coming for the vibe and the cricket.
VO: Why is SA20 so popular with fans? We visit Boland Park to see what goes on behind the scenes.

09 February 2025 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 09 June 2025 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: 6660 SA20 Script Paarl Opening Shots Devino VO: I am excited. We don't often get a final home game in Paarl. VO: My name is Devino Jacobs. I live in Paarl. I am a huge Paarl Royals fan. I can't walk around with no paint. People know me as the paint guy! I am very nervous because it is our final home game. We are going to give 110 percent tonight even if I have to lose my voice tonight because that how purple and pink my heart is!” Quick montage of shots: “We are set for match number 23, Power Royals vs the Durban’s….” Link: Devino is definitely someone special, but he's just one of thousands of fans around the country that have come to support their team at the SA20. And that's what this tournament's about. It's about supporting your team, watching exciting cricket, but most of all, it's about the vibe! Shots “That's a very good shot. Catch, one-handed catch. Oh, have we got something? I think we have got something.” VO1: SA20 has made headlines, big hits, passionate fans and an atmosphere buzzing with energy. So we headed to Paarl in the Western Cape to see for ourselves. Link: When you're this close to the action, it makes you think that you can actually play a team. But my skills stopped at Baker's Cricket. Graeme Smith We've been very clear about our ambitions from the start. We've been open. We've been public about wanting to be the biggest league outside of India. With the growth of Franchise Cricket, we really wanted to be the number one player in the Southern Hemisphere. VO2 SA20 is a professional league with 6 privately owned franchises. Franchise cricket is growing globally with the likes of SA20 and the Indian premier league - the IPL. Unlike traditional domestic cricket, it’s a business—teams sign top local and international players, attract big sponsors, and pack stadiums with fans. SA20 features six teams battling it out in 34 matches over 5 weeks, all fighting for a spot in the playoffs and, ultimately, the grand final. And the stakes? A massive R70 million in prize money. At the helm of it all is former Proteas captain Graeme Smith. Now in its third season, HIS team has been working relentlessly to take SA20 to new heights. Graeme Smith I remember that first World Cup in 07 in South Africa and then IPL kicked off in 08 and I was a part of both and I couldn't believe how suddenly this format just really captured the imagination. For cricket to grow into the future, we needed to start introducing new audiences. So outside putting on the best cricketers in the world and the field, we really did try and change things up and create an in-stadium through the TV experience that people thought was fun, new, fresh and would attract anyone really. There's a product in your own country that people are talking about at a global level. Upsound Got him straight through, Maphaka has struck... Nikhil Uttamchandani What has been developed here is more than just a cricket tournament. The product has now evolved into people. I mean, for us to be in Paarl on a Monday and to be a sell-out crowd, I think that speaks volumes about what the league has done. It's the league of people, I think. VO3: Nikhil Uttamchandani is one of the commentators. Nikhil uttamchandani I often when I'm off commentary tend to just go into the crowd and just stand there, sometimes sit, talk to people, talk to the locals, learn some Afrikaans. It's great man. Yeah, I really enjoy it. VO4: But it's not all fun and games. The SA20 also has a serious side. Players aim to impress with hopes of being selected for the IPL, which is often career changing. Upsound Oh, there's a shout first up. VO5: And making sure the game stays fair, the umpires, often unnoticed, but essential. Govan How does umpiring this kind of tournament differ from normal umpiring? Tom Mokorosi Yeah, so we've got DRS, which is a big change from our domestic cricket, where players can review umpires' decisions. If you make a mistake, it is corrected. The right decision is made and the game moves on. Govan: But it's also nice and dramatic. Tom: The heart rate flies through the roof as soon as they review it. And that first replay comes on. Your onscreen signal now. Upsound What a good start for the Durbans, super giants. They picked up Joe Root. Tom Mokorosi We don't often umpire for packed stadiums. And it definitely is something we want more of, not less of. And the nervousness is good, nervous energy. Graeme Smith One area is our domestic cricket and international cricket. The gap was widening. I think one thing that the SA20 has done is it's closed that gap. You've created almost an international league in South Africa now where our players, both those experienced and young, are being exposed to a platform that hopefully will make them even better cricketers. The other thing is, last year we had the most players picked up at the IPL. And that platform that our players are getting now outside those that played for South Africa, there's a lot that never would have been seen. And now they're being seen and they're getting opportunities globally as well. VO6: One of these young players is Paarl Royals bowler Codi Yusuf. Cody Yousuf I don't think you can come into any of the games and say this team will win or that team will win. All around this, there's very good players in each of the teams. Govan Has the SA20 changed your life at all? Cody Yousuf Definitely. It's obviously given me the exposure financially as well. Obviously there's a lot of money that they pumped into this comp and I managed to do things that I couldn't do before I came into this comp. So it definitely changed my life. VO7: Nqaba Peter is back for HIS second season with the Paarl Royals. Nqaba Peter I never knew at this age I could be such a role model, not just for people younger than me, but also for guys who are even older than me. All the guys come and tell me, listen man, we watch you every time we play, we're rooting for you, we really look up to you. People have kids who want our kids to be like you one day. Govan It's because you represent them. It's very important for black cricket players to get representation time. Nqaba Peter I do think there are black players who are talented and skilled enough to be in the SA20. Graeme Smith We've worked with Cricket South Africa on the structure. The amount of money that they're spending on grassroots programs annually, we're supporting them on schools. I think there's definitely been improvements. We are a global league that splits players up. So there's four international players per every team as well, which takes up an immense amount of playing places as well. It's good to see young black African talent coming through like Maphaka and making that this stage. Every game now we're starting to see really big contributions and hopefully our franchises will recognize that and go from strength to strength. Link The IPL showed us how popular T20 cricket can be, but the SA20 is showing that South Africans can do it too. We certainly have the fans and the vibe! Upsound: That's clubbed. That's a very good shot. Catch, one handed catch. Oh, have we got something? I think we have got something. Link: So one handed catch while I'm here. That's incredible. VO8: Another fan-favorite addition is the one-handed catch competition, with a huge cash prize up for grabs. The rules are simple—catch the ball with one hand, and you’re in the running. At the end of the tournament, all the successful catchers share the R2 million prize! Upsound Oh, he's on his knee and he's clubbed that one and he's hit it for six. What a shot. Govan Three to win from two. VO9: The win alone was enough to send Devino home smiling, but his night was about to get even more special. Not only did he meet his hero, Proteas stalwart David Miller—he even got a team shirt. But knowing Davino, he’ll never wear it… END Promo1 VO: Big names, big hits, and six teams fighting to win it all. Graeme Smith Platform for them globally is huge because now the whole world's watching this. Instead of 15 players touring for their country, there's now 70 that are getting the opportunity for people around the world to see. VO: We attended a few games to find out what makes SA20 so popular. Promo 2 VO: Ever wondered what it takes to run a cricket league? SA20 isn't just about the players. We go behind the scenes to find out what makes this tournament so popular. Nqaba I think SA20 has definitely done a lot for young players. This is the second biggest league in the world. Promos 3 VO: There is a superfan behind every super over! (Alt Take) Graeme Smith There's a level of loyalty of the fans to their teams. It's not just coming for the vibe and the cricket. VO: Why is SA20 so popular with fans? We visit Boland Park to see what goes on behind the scenes.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Imagine a cricket tournament that’s not just about the game. It’s a show. A celebration. A way to show off South Africa’s talent and spirit.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: This is SA20—our country’s top T20 cricket league. But it’s more than big hits and fireworks. It’s about people and their stories. One of these fans is now famous, Devino Jacobs, we follow his journey to Paarl grounds to watch Paarl Royals play Durban's Super Giants! We’ll speak to Graeme Smith, the tournament director. He’s the man behind it all. He tells us first hand how he ended up here, director of the tournament. He’ll share how SA20 started and why it’s about more than just cricket—it’s about uniting South Africans and creating opportunities. We weave stories of players in and out of the main story. Then there’s Codi Yusuf. His cricket career almost ended before it even started. But SA20 gave him a second chance. Now, he’s back, showing that it’s never too late to turn your life around. And Nqaba Peter—he went from practicing at Border to bowling for the Proteas. His story proves that talent can be found anywhere, even in the most unexpected places. We’ll go behind the scenes to see the sacrifices, the hard work, and the dreams that keep these players going. It’s not just about the players. It’s about the umpires, the fans, and everyone who makes SA20 special. We’ll attend a few games and capture our passion for cricket and have some voxies of fans. Bring in the catches and what fans can win - R1million! This league isn’t just cricket. And it’s proof that anyone can rise if given the opportunity. That’s what SA20 is all about. We end the show with our Superfan, Devino - going out of frame happy!
